title.title: Ultraflat $\pm 1$ polynomials exist
title.subtitle: Claim: for every $\varepsilon$ and large $N$, a $\pm1$ polynomial with $(1-\varepsilon)\sqrt N \le |P| \le (1+\varepsilon)\sqrt N$ on the circle

plain: Pick a plus or minus sign for each term so the sum's size stays almost perfectly level around a circle

beats.text: A real $\pm1$ polynomial on the circle: its average size is $\sqrt N$
Rudin–Shapiro signs stay under $\sqrt{2N}$, but swing far from $\sqrt N$
The claim: for every $\varepsilon$, some $\pm1$ signing stays inside the band

steps: Build a smooth curve of constant size from short wave pieces
Make its coefficients almost plus or minus the same size
Round them to exact signs without spoiling the flatness

achievement.label: A fixed gap for every ±1 polynomial (conjectured)
achievement.context: Conjectured by $\text{Erd\H{o}s}$. Before: flat only within constant factors (Annals 2020)
achievement.note: Existential, no rate or algorithm; el Abdalaoui (2025) claims the opposite

verify.detail: Lean: $\max|P| \le (1+\eta)\sqrt N$ and finite-$p$ flatness. Not the two-sided theorem
verify.ourCheck: We computed the Rudin–Shapiro curve shown; we did not run Comparator

voice.text: Plus and minus one coefficients. Their size averages root N; experts doubted it stays level.
Build a flat curve from wave pieces, then round its coefficients to signs.
Claimed: flat within any margin you like.

sources.quote: Balister–Bollobás–Morris–Sahasrabudhe–Tiba, 'Flat Littlewood polynomials exist' (Annals 2020) gives c1√N ≤ |P| ≤ c2√N.
Contrary claim: el Abdalaoui (arXiv:2504.21499, 2025) asserts Littlewood polynomials are not L^α-flat for even α ≥ 4 and no ultraflat sequence exists
NOT formalized: the two-sided ultraflat theorem (3), the √N/16 lower bound (2), and the merit-factor/Morse-shift consequences.
